d016.note: The quotas and timeout pages state 5,400 seconds (90 minutes) for async and event source mapping invocations except Amazon MQ and Amazon DocumentDB. The What's New feed dates Lambda Managed Instances itself 2025-11-30; the 90-minute date (FRESHNESS 2026-09-09) is for the decisions+changes lens to confirm.

d023.contradiction: The developer guide quotas page says 300 GB is 'Not increasable'; the General Reference quotas table (docs/general/latest/gr/lambda-service, row 'Function and layer storage') lists 300 Gigabytes as Adjustable: Yes. The developer guide is taken as current truth.

d025.not_found: The old account-wide burst limits (500 to 3,000 per Region) are not stated on any saved guide page.
d025.contradiction: lambda-concurrency page, section 'Understanding concurrency and requests per second', says 'A function using on-demand concurrency can experience a burst increase of 500 concurrency every 10 seconds, or by 5,000 requests per second every 10 seconds, whichever happens first.' The same page's scaling-rate section, scaling-behavior, the quotas page and the General Reference all say 1,000 every 10 seconds. No fact was added for the 500 example.

d033.contradiction: The decision guide docs/decision-guides/latest/decision-guides/fargate-or-lambda says 'ENIs are an exhaustible resource with a soft limit of 250 per Region.' The Lambda quotas page and the General Reference say 3,000 elastic network interfaces per VPC. The quotas pages are current truth; no fact was added for 250.

d035.note: The General Reference lists no separate Invoke API rate; invocation is limited by concurrency (10 requests per second per environment for synchronous calls).

d039.note: The 60-second minimum is stated only in the API reference (Valid Range: Minimum value of 60. Maximum value of 21600.); the developer guide says 'up to 6 hours'. The default of 6 hours is stated as a default only for throttling and system-error retries (lambda-async-throttle-retry-6-hours).

d044.contradiction: Expected a ceiling of 1,000 batches; services-sqs-scaling says one event source mapping can process up to 1,250 concurrent invokes (100,000 in provisioned mode). Start of five batches and up to 300 more concurrent invokes per minute match.
